- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply 3–5% downward bias to first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits high variance; use 50% of recent 7-day average as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0, model often fails to adjust downward; apply 5–10% downward correction for next 3–5 days.
